evidence: Gell. 17.8.8: nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?
Plin. NH 9.169: petere Brundisium ostreās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of going somewhere for something (Lewis & Short). “Bring it here” is affer (bring).
Of making someone come (Lewis & Short): medicum arcessere, to fetch the doctor.

phrases.latin: verberō … nōnne īs curriculō atque oleum petis?
phrases.english: You rascal … won’t you run and get some oil?

phrases.latin: ībō atque accersam medicum jam quantum potest.
phrases.english: I’ll go and fetch the doctor, as fast as I can.
to summon, call someone to oneself

sources: Lewis & Short: peto · Lewis & Short: arcesso
